_meta.indication: Radioactive diagnostic agent indicated for PET of PSMA-positive lesions in men with prostate cancer with suspected metastasis who are candidates for initial definitive therapy, or with suspected recurrence based on elevated serum PSA.

pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, single-arm, open-label, multicenter trial assessing flotufolastat F 18 PET/CT against a histopathology reference standard from radical prostatectomy and pelvic lymph node dissection.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with newly diagnosed unfavorable intermediate-risk, high-risk, or very high-risk prostate cancer who were candidates for radical prostatectomy and pelvic lymph node dissection.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints of patient-level sensitivity and patient-level specificity of flotufolastat F 18 PET/CT for detection of pelvic lymph node metastases against histopathology.
pivotal_trials.n: 356 enrolled; 296 evaluable for pelvic lymph node histopathology.
pivotal_trials.result: Specificity high (93%, 94%, 97% across three readers) but sensitivity low (30%, 27%, 23%); PPV 57%, 58%, 70%. The specificity threshold was met by all readers, but the co-primary sensitivity threshold was not met.

pivotal_trials.design: Prospective, single-arm, open-label, multicenter trial assessing flotufolastat F 18 PET/CT against a composite reference standard of histopathology and imaging.
pivotal_trials.population: Men with suspected biochemical recurrence of prostate cancer based on elevated serum PSA (>=0.2 ng/mL after prostatectomy, or nadir +2 ng/mL after other therapies) eligible for salvage therapy.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Co-primary endpoints of patient-level correct detection rate (CDR) and region-level positive predictive value (PPV) against a composite reference standard.
pivotal_trials.n: 391 enrolled; 389 with an evaluable POSLUMA PET scan.
pivotal_trials.result: Patient-level CDR met its threshold (54.1%, 51.4%, 51.6%; majority read 56.8%; all p<0.0001 vs H0 CDR<=36.5%), but co-primary region-level PPV did not meet the 62.5% goal (46.2%, 60.3%, 52.6%; majority read 59.7%).

key_safety: Adverse reactions were uncommon and typically mild. In N=747, the most common adverse reactions (>=0.4%) were diarrhea (0.7%), blood pressure increase (0.5%), and injection site pain (0.4%).
target_moa: Flotufolastat F 18 binds to PSMA (IC50 = 4.4 nM) expressed on prostate cancer cells and is internalized; the fluorine-18 beta+ emitting radionuclide is detected by PET.

rems.type: REMS are not needed for flotufolastat F 18.

companion_dx_detail: Devices and Companion Diagnostic Issues section not applicable to this NDA.

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee meetings were held; the application was not referred because the drug is not the first in its class.

summary.text: Standard review 505(b)(1) NDA received May 25, 2022 with a May 25, 2023 PDUFA goal date; priority review was requested but denied given availability of other products in this class. The application was approved as a traditional (not accelerated) approval, was not referred to an advisory committee, and required no REMS or postmarketing requirements/commitments.
